title: Income-Based Travel Support — RideLink Meal Supplement Schedule
content:
Members of lower household income receive a meal supplement on top of the daily meals allowance during a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation long-distance stay.

**Rule.** A meal supplement is added to each meal day's allowance by the household income the member's active Medicaid Managed Care Membership records: at or below the deep-poverty percent of 50 percent of the federal poverty level, the deep-poverty meal supplement of 6.50 USD; above 50 percent and at or below the poverty percent of 100 percent, the poverty meal supplement of 3.25 USD; above 100 percent, no supplement.

The supplement is added to the daily meals allowance, so it is paid on every meal day the stay counts, in the same measure as the allowance itself. The income figure is the household income, as a percent of the federal poverty level, recorded on the member's active membership.

## Income bands

| Recorded household income (percent of the federal poverty level) | Meal supplement per meal day |
|---|---|
| 50 or below | 6.50 USD |
| Above 50, up to and including 100 | 3.25 USD |
| Above 100 | None |

## Boundary rows

| Hypothetical recorded income | Supplement |
|---|---|
| 50 percent | 6.50 USD |
| 50.1 percent | 3.25 USD |
| 100 percent | 3.25 USD |
| 100.1 percent | None |

*Worked figure, hypothetical:* for 3 meal days at a recorded income of 80 percent, the supplement adds 3 times 3.25, that is 9.75 USD, to the meals.
